title: Static-W anti-Hermitian residual is inherited from a non-Hermitian chi, not produced by the Coulomb screening code
symptom: Job 3250730 failed at the iq28 static-W gate: the positive/negative pairing test passes at 1.125e-15, but static W has Hermres 1.536e-11, above the 1e-11 limit. The input static chi already has Hermres 4.0337e-12 while the Coulomb roots are Hermitian to ~1e-16.
root_cause: For Wc = T Y S chi S Y^dag T with Hermitian Coulomb roots S,T and Y = (I - S chi S)^-1, the anti-Hermitian part of static Wc is exactly T Y S (chi - chi^dag) S Y^dag T. This was verified numerically: the C++ W anti-Hermitian part matches that expression to 3.64e-16 absolute, and the C++ W itself agrees with an independent general complex solve to 2.14e-15. The 1.5e-11 residual therefore comes from the upstream chi producer.
minimal_fix: Leave the static-W gate and the C++ screening untouched and move the investigation to the chi producer, which already carries ~4e-12 anti-Hermitian weight; fix the producer so chi is Hermitian to the required tolerance.
validation: Check element-wise that W - W^dag equals T Y S (chi - chi^dag) S Y^dag T (expect ~1e-16 agreement) and that the C++ W matches an independent general LU solve to ~1e-15; then re-run the iq28 static gate after the producer fix and require Hermres <= 1e-11.
avoid: Do not Hermitian-project W, do not relax the 1e-11 threshold, and do not treat the failing q point as a bug in the screening algorithm — the attribution algebra shows where the asymmetry enters.
